subject: ParityPay budget & pilot scope — reconciliation and next steps
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@paritypay.com>, Rajesh Patel <rajesh.p@paritypay.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: ParityPay discovery — budget & pilot scope recap

Hi Emma / Rajesh — thanks again for a productive call this morning. Quick written recap so we have aligned asks and so your procurement team has a clean description for budgeting.

Key pain & goals you confirmed
- Latency-sensitive fraud review flows that currently call multiple internal models and external lookups; average session is ~350 tokens of LLM work per event.
- Current cloud spend target: keep inference incremental spend under $25k/month for initial pilot runway (3 months).
- Must maintain PCI-compliant data handling and in-region hosting for US customers.

What we proposed (summary)
1) Pilot scope: 2-model serving (ranker + explanation) behind Redwood Dedicated pool. Target throughput: 50 RPS average, 150 RPS peak.
2) Cost levers we discussed: sequence-length trimming, adaptive batching (50–128 token buckets), prefix KV caching for user histories, and quantized model variant for high-throughput paths.
3) Rough TCO math we walked through on call:
   - Baseline token-rate estimate: 1M tokens/day -> ~30M tokens/month.
   - Expected per-token unit cost (hosted-equivalent via pilot config): ~$0.0009 per token without batching/caching; with conservative batching+cache expect ~30–45% savings depending on hit rate.
   - Ballpark pilot compute + infra reserve: $15k–$22k/month depending on autoscale headroom.

Open items / clarifications we need from you
- Confirmation of the 3-month pilot budget ceiling (you mentioned $25k/month) — please confirm if that is firm or a target.
- Typical session length distribution (p50/p95 token counts) to better size batching thresholds. You said you could share anonymized logs.
- Procurement contacts and any template SOW clauses for data residency.

Attachments & links
- Attached: paritypay-pilot-sizing.xlsx (pilot sizing workbook) and paritypay-sow-draft.pdf (starter SOW).
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/3456789

Recommended next steps (minimal friction path)
1) You confirm budget ceiling and share session token distribution (ETA: 2 business days).
2) Redwood provides a tuned pilot config (batch sizes, cache TTL, quantization profile) + expected monthly cost ranges (ETA: 2 business days after we get token distribution).
3) If numbers align, we run a 3-month pilot on Dedicated with a 30% cache hit assumption baseline; we deliver a cost/vs-quality dashboard and a short retro at month 3.

Would you like us to turn the pilot sizing workbook into a 30-minute walkthrough for your engineering/procurement teams next week?

Thanks — appreciate the time.

Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
dylan@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0147

---
Attachment: paritypay-pilot-sizing.xlsx (xlsx)
Attachment: paritypay-sow-draft.pdf (pdf)
From: Emma Li <emma.li@paritypay.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajesh Patel <rajesh.p@paritypay.com>, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 13:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ParityPay discovery — budget & pilot scope recap

Thanks Dylan — good write-up and captures the call clearly. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Budget: $25k/month is our committed ceiling for Q3 pilot spend. We have flexibility to push to $28k/month if the case on ROI looks strong and we can show clear reduction in manual review overhead.
2) Logs: I will extract anonymized token-length distribution (p50/p95) and share by Monday. Expect p50 ~ 320 tokens, p95 ~ 980 tokens for fraud review sessions.
3) Data residency: procurement requires US-only hosting and a SOC 2 attestation (you mentioned Redwood has SOC 2 Type II — can you attach the latest report or a SOC2 letter?).

One ask: can you include a sensitivity table in the sizing workbook showing cost outcomes at caching hit rates of 10%, 30%, and 50%? That will help our CFO model downside.

If you can send the SOC2 docs and the sensitivity table, I’ll route to procurement and Sales Ops for a fast-track review. Happy to do the 30-minute walkthrough — Tue or Wed next week prefered.

Best,
Emma Li
Head of ML Ops, ParityPay
emma.li@paritypay.com | +1 617-555-0231
From: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 1 May 2027 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: ParityPay discovery — budget & pilot scope recap

Quick internal note — Emma asked for the SOC 2 report and the sensitivity table (10/30/50% cache hit). I can take the SOC2 packaging and push to compliance; could you own the sensitivity table (I can help with numbers once you have the p50/p95)? Also, liaison with procurement will likely ask for an expedited SOW signature path — flagging legal.

If we keep base pilot at $25k/mo (they said ceiling) we should prepare a conservative runbook for autoscale limits and a fallback to quantized model to protect runway. I’ll draft the suggested fallback language for the SOW.

-Lauren
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai

Date: Sat, 1 May 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ParityPay discovery — budget & pilot scope recap

Emma — great, thank you for the quick turn. Plan from our side: 

1) I’ll populate the sensitivity table (10/30/50% cache hit) and add a conservative autoscale headroom scenario for $25k vs $28k ceilings. Expect spreadsheet update by EOD Monday.
2) Lauren will attach SOC2 Type II summary and the short compliance package to the Hub link (Lauren — appreciate the handoff).
3) Proposed walkthrough: Tue 10:00am PT (30 minutes) — covers sizing workbook, runbook, and SOW-ish acceptance criteria. Please confirm.

Immediate asks for you: 
- Procurement contact or procurement SOW template if you want us to align to your clause language.
- The anonymized token distribution export (p50/p95) when you have it Monday.

If all good, I’ll update HubSpot (PAR-3247) with the confirmed budget ceiling and schedule the walkthrough.

Thanks again — looking forward to getting a tight pilot that proves runway and unit-econ improvements.

Dylan Brooks
